svg.aria-label: Three radar charts with the ten spokes of the upscaler comparison's chart and on its scale: on every spoke the best of the five upscalers compared there reaches the outer ring. Left: this project's exact DLL, with the steady test as a dashed outline. Middle: the steady test, right: the community bias DLL, each with the exact DLL as a dashed outline. The three shapes are nearly the same; the steady test reaches further at rest, the bias DLL is shorter on the wire and on speed. Still picture and moving background, mean: accuracy (dB): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 46.80 dB, Steady test (this project) 46.89 dB, Community bias DLL (0.5) 46.77 dB. Thin railing in motion: accuracy (dB): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 41.82 dB, Steady test (this project) 41.82 dB, Community bias DLL (0.5) 41.76 dB. Areas a moving object has just uncovered, mean of a panning and a still camera: accuracy (dB): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 33.55 dB, Steady test (this project) 33.51 dB, Community bias DLL (0.5) 33.53 dB. Old image beside a moving object, mean of seven scenes: error (of 255): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 1.92, Steady test (this project) 1.96, Community bias DLL (0.5) 2.01. Thin bars fixed on screen in front of a panning background, mean of four pans: error where their old image lands (of 255): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 0.82, Steady test (this project) 0.83, Community bias DLL (0.5) 0.86. Tiny fast sparks: share of their brightness shown (%): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 83%, Steady test (this project) 83%, Community bias DLL (0.5) 83%. Leaves swaying without motion vectors, mean of three sway speeds: error (of 255): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 11.0, Steady test (this project) 11.1, Community bias DLL (0.5) 11.5. Still picture: change per frame (of 255): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 0.037, Steady test (this project) 0.026, Community bias DLL (0.5) 0.035. Thin wire under a slow pan: how close its brightness is to the true one (%): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 90.5%, Steady test (this project) 90.9%, Community bias DLL (0.5) 85.3%. Time per upscale call, mean of 1080p, 1440p and 4K output (ms): Exact DLL (AMD's picture) 1.83 ms, Steady test (this project) 1.84 ms, Community bias DLL (0.5) 2.67 ms.
svg.text: The three on the upscaler comparison's scale
The ten spokes of that page's chart; the outer ring is the best of its five upscalers. Bigger is better.
Dashed: the exact DLL (left: the steady test). Old image: seven scenes; fixed bars: four pans; foliage: three sway speeds; speed: mean of 1080p, 1440p, 4K.
Speed: Windows timing kit under Proton, the three in one run. The bias DLL runs AMD's own shaders, so it has AMD's speed.
Test rig, 4K output from 2260x1272, Radeon RX 7800 XT, single runs, auto exposure off. Neither test build has been tried in a game.
